transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
President Trump's campaign sprint takes him to Alaska today.
The 3,400-mile trip is to help Republican Senator Dan Sullivan fend off a challenge
from Democratic former Congresswoman Mary Paltola, whose campaign has emphasized affordability
issues and appears Franco Ordonez has more.
The president continues to struggle in the polls, but he insists his campaign appearances
are helping Republicans in competitive races.
The White House says Trump's travel schedule will only intensify over the next few weeks,
leading up to the midterms.
He has stops planned in Georgia, Kentucky and Florida.
The president has focused largely on red states, as the campaign seeks to boost enthusiasm
with his base.
But political strategists warn Trump may actually be doing more harm for his party by stirring
up opposition, Franco Ordonez and PR News, the White House.
President Trump's ambassador to Greece, Kimberly Guilfoyle, has stepped down amid reports of
misconduct.
She says she will defend herself, and she thanked Trump for what she called an honor
of a lifetime, as NPR's Michelle Kellerman reports.
President Trump says he didn't even talk to Guilfoyle, who was once engaged to his eldest
son.
I did speak to her now, but she will not be there.
I didn't like what I read.
Guilfoyle faces numerous allegations, including that she urged a Trump donor to pay off a
$100,000 credit card bill in exchange for access to the administration.
She says she will vigorously defend her name and reputation.
The ranking Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, Gregory Meeks, is calling
for continued investigations, saying, quote, "serving as a U.S. ambassador is a position
of public trust, not a business opportunity."
Michelle Kellerman, NPR News, the State Department.
The housing market remains in a slump.
Existing home sales in September rose from August, but sales were down from a year earlier.
NPR's Stephen Masaha reports mortgage rates are near a three-year high.
The only month slower for home sales in September was August, after making adjustments for seasons.
The National Association of Realtors says this is not a supply issue.
Homes available for sale are at their pre-COVID levels.
Instead, it's about high mortgage rates.
In September, the average for the 30-year fixed-rate mortgage rose past 6.8 percent.
Since September, rates have only climbed.
Last week, mortgage rates reached a near three-year high of 7.4 percent.
It could go even higher if the Federal Reserve hikes its benchmark interest rate again in
the coming months.
Stephen Masaha, NPR News, Birmingham, Alabama.
Pope Leo XIV has lung cancer and had the lower lobe of his right lung removed.
A surgery today confirmed a diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma.
The 71-year-old was in the operating room for about three hours with the surgery lasting
90 minutes.
Oncologists say his prognosis is excellent since it was removed early.
This is NPR News from Washington.
Grocery store chain Kroger says it will lay off 3,000 corporate employees over the next
three years as it ramps up its use of AI to streamline operations.
Kroger is based in Cincinnati.
It's the largest standalone U.S. supermarket chain with 409,000 employees and more than
2,700 stores operating under brands such as Ralph's, King Scoopers, Smith's and Fred
Meyer.
NASA's Mars Rover, Perseverance, just logged a major milestone, the longest total drive
distance by a vehicle on another world.
Here's NPR's Ari Daniel.
That distance is 28 miles, which may not seem like much by earthly standards, but project
scientist Katie Stack Morgan says it's a big deal for an off-world rover.
This is the culmination of how we explore the solar system and the capabilities that
we bring to other planets.
Over the last half-decade, Perseverance has collected possible evidence of life in Jezero
Crater and sampled rocks that might represent the first half-billion years of solar system
history.
It collected material from the Martian surface so that one day another mission might return
those samples to Earth.
But this part of the program has an uncertain future, given its hefty price tag put it in
the crosshairs of the federal government earlier this year.
Ari Daniel, NPR News.
Israel has returned 22 ancient Greek artifacts that were illegally removed from Greece, marking
the first such repatriation between the two countries.
The collection includes a bronze statuette with a woman and pottery decorated with mythological
scenes and geometric motifs dating from approximately 700 to 320 B.C.
This message comes from IXL, a learning platform for helping kids build confidence and get
up to speed fast.
One subscription covers math, science, and reading for all children in a household.
Receive 20% off at IXL.com/NPR.

topics.text: President Trump travels to Alaska to help Senator Dan Sullivan against Mary Peltola
Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle steps down amid reports of misconduct
Existing home sales rise from August but fall from a year earlier amid high mortgage rates
Pope Leo XIV undergoes surgery to remove lower lobe of right lung after lung cancer diagnosis
Kroger to lay off 3,000 corporate employees over three years as it expands AI use
NASA's Perseverance rover logs record 28-mile total drive distance on Mars
Israel returns 22 illegally removed ancient Greek artifacts to Greece in first such repatriation
